input.question: Why are there so many different kinds of cheese made from cow's milk, but cheese made from goat's milk is just "goat cheese".
input.ground_truth: It isn't just "goat cheese", it's just that your average American doesn't have enough experiences with goat cheeses to name any particular one. Feta, Kunik, Castelo Branco, and Clochette are all (at least partially) goat cheese that I've eaten personally. I'd think that pretty much everyone in the US has some experience with feta at a minimum.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: Why are there so many different kinds of cheese made from cow's milk, but cheese made from goat's milk is just "goat cheese".

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have a big box of red crayons and you can make lots of different pictures with them—like flowers, houses, and stars. That’s like cow’s milk cheese. People have made so many different kinds of cheese from cow’s milk because they’ve been using cow’s milk for a very, very long time, and they’ve tried lots of ways to make it taste different or look different.

But now, imagine you only have one green crayon. You can make a lot of things with it, but most of the time, people just call it “green crayon” because there’s not as many ways to change it. That’s like goat’s milk cheese. People usually just call it “goat cheese” because there aren’t as many different kinds made from goat’s milk, and it’s a bit harder to make lots of different types. But that doesn’t mean goat cheese isn’t yummy! It’s just simpler to call it “goat cheese.”
